# Security: Audits, Remediation, AIDefence/TEE, Hash & Hailo Hardening

## What was decided

Implement defense-in-depth security across four layers: (1) critical vulnerability remediation in core Rust/Metal/shell code, (2) AIDefence multi-layer prompt injection/jailbreak/PII detection, (3) TEE hardware root-of-trust with SGX/SEV-SNP/TDX attestation, and (4) constant-time hash verification with SHAKE-256 cryptographic integrity. All critical findings fixed before production; high/medium issues tracked with remediation timelines.

## Why this approach

Industry-standard single-layer security (authentication-only, or perimeter firewalls) fails against supply-chain attacks and prompt injection. Rejected alternatives: (a) API-only rate limiting—bypassed via key rotation without IP-based quotas; (b) XXH3-128-only hashing—no cryptographic preimage resistance; (c) panic-based error handling—enables allocation DoS attacks. Constant-time comparison (via `subtle` crate) prevents timing side-channels that non-cryptographic hashes don't defend against. TEE attestation binds keys to hardware measurements, preventing credential theft across VM/container boundaries.

## When to apply

- **Production LLM deployments** requiring jailbreak/PII protection—AIDefence adds <5ms latency for 30+ threat patterns.
- **Federated transfer scenarios** (ADR-057) where segment integrity must survive MITM—use SHAKE-256 keyed hashing (algo=3).
- **Multi-tenant clusters** on Hailo NPUs—apply mTLS + IP-based rate limiting + per-peer governor to prevent resource exhaustion.
- **Edge/IoT constrained environments**—hardened Linux microkernel + eBPF syscall filters eliminate 90% attack surface vs full distros.
- **Shared brain servers** (π.ruv.io)—15-rule PII stripper + IP vote dedup stops Sybil quality score manipulation.

## What's unique

Combines hardware TEE attestation with semantic-agnostic threat detection (ADR-042's 5-layer AIDefence operates pre-embedding, blocking attacks before they reach the model) and witness-chain tamper evidence. Hailo NPU workers enforce Ed25519 manifest signing on discovery files—supply-chain defense at the edge hardware layer, not just software.

## Reference ADRs

- ADR-007: Security review identified 8 critical vulnerabilities—Metal shader overflows, GGUF integer overflows, race conditions—all fixed with safety documentation ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-007-security-review-technical-debt.md))
- ADR-012: Command injection prevention via regex allowlisting, panic-to-Result conversion for allocation failures, shell script hardening ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-012-security-remediation.md))
- ADR-042: AIDefence + TEE hardened cognitive container—5-layer adversarial defense, SGX/SEV-SNP attestation, KernelBinding anti-tamper ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-042-Security-RVF-AIDefence-TEE.md))
- ADR-058: Constant-time hash verification, SHAKE-256 implementation, removed dead CRC32C code, reserved algo=3 for HMAC ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-058-hash-security-optimization.md))
- ADR-073: π.ruv.io platform audit—PI key in URL path fixed via SHAKE-256 pseudonym, IP-based rate limiting, edge genesis 404 handling ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-073-pi-platform-security-optimization.md))
- ADR-079: SQL audit script hardening—dollar quoting fixes, fault-tolerant DO blocks, programmatic PASS/FAIL verdicts ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-079-sql-audit-script-hardening.md))
- ADR-082: Brain server PII expansion (phone/SSN/credit card), IP-based vote dedup with 24h TTL, Sybil-resistant quality scoring ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-082-brain-security-hardening.md))
- ADR-114: HashEmbedding marked as placeholder—RuvLLM ONNX provides real semantic embeddings, ApiEmbedding fallback documented ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-114-ruvector-core-hash-placeholders.md))

title: Coherence Engine: Gated Transformer, Kernel Integration

# Coherence Engine: Gated Transformer, Kernel Integration

## What was decided
The Coherence Engine uses sheaf Laplacian mathematics to compute edge-level residuals and aggregate them into coherence energy scores that gate compute depth and action safety. Transformer attention is replaced with coherence-gated routing (reflex/standard/deep lanes based on residual energy), and the kernel auto-feeds IPC traffic into a live coherence graph with 5% per-epoch decay, propagating scores to scheduler priority and driving split/merge decisions through capability-checked operations.

## Why this approach
Standard transformers waste O(N²) compute on all tokens equally and rely on unreliable confidence scores for early exit. Flash Attention and sparse patterns (local, strided) don't adapt to content; linear attention degrades quality. Sheaf residuals provide mathematical consistency proofs rather than probabilistic guesses, routing compute only where structural contradictions exist. Kernel integration via IPC auto-feeding eliminates manual instrumentation while edge decay prevents stale topology from corrupting decisions—an improvement over static analysis tools that ignore temporal dynamics.

## When to apply
- LLM inference where hallucination refusal requires provable witnesses, not confidence thresholds
- Agent systems with multi-partition communication where coherence energy must drive scheduler priority and split/merge topology changes
- Real-time workloads needing <0.1ms reflex lane for coherent tokens and 5ms deep lane only for high-residual outliers
- Security-sensitive environments requiring capability-gated structural operations with mandatory audit trails
- Any domain (finance, robotics, medical) where "does the world still fit together?" matters more than "what will happen next?"

## What's unique
Coherence is a continuously updated field computed from restriction map residuals, not a learned heuristic. The same sheaf Laplacian object interprets as hallucination energy in LLMs, regime mismatch in finance, motion impossibility in robotics, or authorization violations in security—zero domain-specific rewrites.

## Reference ADRs
- ADR-014: Coherence Engine Architecture—sheaf Laplacian foundation, universal coherence object, domain-agnostic interpretation ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-014-coherence-engine.md))
- ADR-015: Coherence-Gated Transformer—sheaf attention, restriction map projections, token-level compute routing ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-015-coherence-gated-transformer.md))

title: Coherence Engine Deep Architecture (22 ADRs): Sheaf Laplacians, Storage, Governance, Compute Ladders

# Coherence Engine Deep Architecture (22 ADRs): Sheaf Laplacians, Storage, Governance, Compute Ladders

## What was decided

Prime-Radiant's coherence engine uses sheaf Laplacian energy E(S) = Σ w_e|r_e|² as a mathematical coherence witness, not probabilistic confidence scores. A four-lane compute ladder (Reflex <1ms → Retrieval ~10ms → Heavy ~100ms → Human async) escalates only on sustained incoherence. Storage splits: PostgreSQL for ACID governance (PolicyBundles, signed WitnessRecords, LineageRecords), ruvector for vector/graph operations. All events append to a signed hash-chain log enabling deterministic replay.

## Why this approach

Traditional confidence scores can be confidently wrong (hallucination). Sheaf energy provides structural proof: zero energy means perfect global consistency, non-zero localizes exact contradictions via residuals r_e = ρ_u(x_u) - ρ_v(x_v). Rejected probabilistic gating (no guarantees), single-tier compute (either too slow or too lenient), and monolithic storage (either weak ACID or poor vector performance). The domain-agnostic substrate (one sheaf object, multiple interpretations) beats building separate systems per domain. Incremental computation with cached residuals and subgraph summaries reduces updates from O(|E|) to O(degree × d).

## When to apply

- **Multi-domain systems** where AI beliefs, financial trades, medical vitals, or security policies need unified coherence checking
- **Compliance-critical applications** requiring tamper-evident audit trails, multi-party approval, and deterministic replay of all decisions
- **High-throughput systems** where most operations must stay <1ms but rare coherence violations need graduated escalation to human review
- **Adaptive systems** that learn from production traces (threshold autotuning, failure patterns → restriction maps) while maintaining governance control
- **RuvLLM integration** where CoherenceValidator, ConfidenceChecker, and memory layers need mathematical grounding instead of heuristics

## What's unique

Sheaf-theoretic coherence witness is provable and localizable (exact edge causing inconsistency), not a statistical guess. Single coherence object serves all domains via restriction map design—once the math is fixed, everything is interpretation.

title: Delta Behavior DDD: Encoding, Propagation, Conflict Resolution, Compression
content:
# Delta Behavior DDD: Encoding, Propagation, Conflict Resolution, Compression

## What was decided
RuVector adopts a delta-first architecture where all vector mutations are expressed as immutable, causally-ordered deltas stored in append-only logs. Vectors are composed on-read from delta chains with periodic checkpoints, enabling temporal queries, efficient replication, and CRDT-based conflict resolution across distributed replicas.

## Why this approach
Full-vector replacement (traditional vector DB approach) requires transmitting entire vectors and rebuilding indexes on every update. Delta-first reduces network bandwidth by 5-20x via sparse encoding and compression, enables git-like temporal versioning impossible with mark-delete semantics, and provides deterministic conflict resolution through vector clocks and LWW/max-value strategies. Alternatives rejected: operational transforms (too complex for numerical data), event sourcing without compaction (unbounded storage growth), snapshot-only versioning (no incremental updates).

## When to apply
- Vectors updated frequently (>1 edit/minute) where network/storage efficiency matters
- Multi-writer scenarios requiring conflict resolution (collaborative embeddings, distributed training)
- Temporal queries needed (rollback, A/B testing historical embeddings, audit trails)
- Geo-distributed deployments where full-vector replication is cost-prohibitive
- Real-time systems requiring <10ms delta propagation with backpressure control

## What's unique
Delta chains use hybrid sparse/dense/RLE encoding with adaptive switching based on change ratio, achieving 3-50x compression. HNSW indexes apply lazy repair with quality bounds rather than immediate rebuilds, maintaining >90% recall while deferring expensive graph restructuring until empirical quality degrades.

## Reference ADRs

title: Quantum Engine: VQE, Grover, QAOA, Surface Codes, Tensor Networks

# Quantum Engine: VQE, Grover, QAOA, Surface Codes, Tensor Networks

## What was decided
Pure Rust state-vector quantum simulator (ruqu-core) compiling to native and WASM, with event-driven activation: zero memory when idle, allocate 2^n complex amplitudes on-demand, execute gates via SIMD-optimized matrix multiplication, deallocate immediately. Supports 25 qubits in WASM (512 MB state vector), 30+ qubits native, with optional tensor network mode for low-entanglement circuits.

## Why this approach
Rejected Qiskit (Python FFI breaks WASM), Cirq (no WASM path), and QuEST (C dependency). Pure Rust ensures memory safety, single build system, and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` compilation without emscripten. State-vector chosen over stabilizer simulation (limited gate set) and pure tensor networks (complex contraction ordering). Direct amplitude manipulation enables O(1) Grover oracles and exact VQE expectation values impossible on real hardware.

## When to apply
- VQE ground-state calculations (8-20 qubits, 50-500 gate depth per iteration) when exact expectation values matter more than hardware fidelity
- Grover search benchmarks where index-based oracles bypass O(n²) gate decomposition
- QAOA on graphs up to 25 nodes when tensor network backend exploits bounded treewidth
- Surface code decoder validation (distance 3-7) with mid-circuit measurement and syndrome extraction
- Browser-based quantum education or agent-driven circuit exploration requiring sandboxed execution

## What's unique
Index-based oracle flips (O(1) vs O(n²) gates), native Rzz gates for QAOA phase separation, mid-circuit measurement with partial collapse, min-cut syndrome decoding integration, and cross-backend verification with cryptographic audit trails. Unified codebase supports embedded (Cognitum 256-core), browser (WASM), and HPC (AVX-512) from identical source.

## Reference ADRs
- ADR-QE-001: Core architecture — state vector vs alternatives, qubit limits, event-driven model ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/quantum/ADR-QE-001-quantum-engine-core-architecture.md))

title: Temporal Tensor Compression: Block Storage, Tiered Quantization, Delta Reconstruction, WASM API
content:
# Temporal Tensor Compression: Block Storage, Tiered Quantization, Delta Reconstruction, WASM API

## What was decided
A five-tier block-based storage engine for streaming tensor data that combines access-frequency-driven quantization (8-bit hot, 7/5-bit warm, 3-bit cold, zero-bit evicted, zero-bit absent), temporal scale reuse across consecutive frames, deterministic 16KB/32KB blocks with CRC32 checksums, sparse delta chains for incremental updates, and a trait-based WASM API with host-delegated I/O. Tier migration uses a composite score (EMA access rate + sliding-window popcount + exponential recency) with hysteresis to prevent thrashing.

## Why this approach
Rejected per-frame quantization (ADR-004 KV cache) due to metadata overhead and lack of temporal reuse. Rejected variable-length segment-only storage (ADR-017 original) due to unpredictable I/O and inability to evict sub-segment granularity. Rejected codebook-based methods (product quantization, AQLM) due to training latency incompatible with streaming workloads. Fixed blocks provide predictable I/O, independent checksums, and tier-granular eviction. Delta chains avoid full rewrites for incremental changes (fine-tuning, embedding updates) while bounded depth prevents O(history) reconstruction cost.

## When to apply
- KV cache tensors in agent workloads with Zipfian access patterns (hot subset <10% of total).
- Embedding streams or attention intermediates where distributions remain stable across 10-100 consecutive frames, enabling scale amortization.
- Memory-constrained deployments requiring <2 bytes/token with bounded reconstruction error.
- Cross-platform tensor stores needing identical WASM semantics on Node.js, browser, and native with host-controlled persistence (IndexedDB, AgentDB, mmap).
- Workloads requiring audit trails or replay where full deletion is unacceptable but zero-cost eviction is mandatory.

## What's unique
Combines temporal scale reuse (H.264-style I-frame/P-frame model applied to quantization parameters) with access-pattern-driven bit-width selection and bounded-depth delta reconstruction, targeting streaming inference rather than static model compression. No prior system addresses all three simultaneously.

## Reference ADRs
- ADR-017: Temporal tensor compression with tiered quantization and groupwise scale reuse ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-017-temporal-tensor-compression.md))
- ADR-018: Block-based storage engine with fixed-size blocks, metadata log, tier buckets (superseded by ADR-029 RVF) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/temporal/ADR-018-block-based-storage-engine.md))
- ADR-019: Concrete bit-packing layouts for 8/7/5/3-bit quantization formats (now rvf-quant) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/temporal/ADR-019-tiered-quantization-formats.md))
- ADR-020: Composite scoring (EMA + popcount + recency) and hysteresis-protected tier migration (now RVF adaptive temperature) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/temporal/ADR-020-temporal-scoring-tier-migration.md))
- ADR-021: Sparse delta encoding and reconstruction policies (None/Delta/Factor; now RVF OVERLAY_SEG) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/temporal/ADR-021-delta-compression-reconstruction.md))
- ADR-022: WASM FFI surface (tts_* exports, host-imported I/O, u128 tensor_id splitting) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/temporal/ADR-022-wasm-api-cross-platform.md))
- ADR-023: Acceptance criteria (Zipf workload, <2us Tier-1 dequant, <0.1 churn/block/min) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/temporal/ADR-023-benchmarking-acceptance-criteria.md))

title: Common Crawl Temporal Compression Pipeline
content:
# Common Crawl Temporal Compression Pipeline

## What was decided

Build a three-phase compressed web memory service that ingests Common Crawl WET files, applies PiQ3 quantization (8.68x compression, 99% recall), spectral sparsification (27-40x edge reduction), and temporal delta tracking to create a queryable semantic memory layer. Start with 500 medical/CS pages/day at $11-28/month, scaling to 10K pages/day at $158-308/month only after validating compression and cost metrics at each tier.

## Why this approach

CDX-based HTML extraction was abandoned because archived HTML structure is inconsistent across decades; WET files provide pre-extracted plain text with 100x faster processing. PiQ3 quantization was chosen over standard quantization after empirical validation showed 8.68x compression with 99% recall. Spectral sparsification prevents MinCut partition timeouts on graphs exceeding 100K edges—tested at 565K edges with 39.8x compression. Historical crawl comparison (quarterly snapshots 2020-2026) enables concept birth detection and narrative fracture analysis, not just static retrieval.

## When to apply

- Build agent shared memory over billion-page corpora where repeated frontier model calls are cost-prohibitive
- Track concept drift, consensus formation, or narrative fractures over time (e.g., medical guideline evolution 2020-2026)
- Detect when topics stabilize, domains shift stance, or new treatments emerge via temporal attractor deltas
- Implement competitive intelligence or trend monitoring requiring cheap multi-tenant retrieval over massive datasets
- Replace expensive always-on vector search clusters with compressed semantic memory and cached partition results

## What's unique

Combines PiQ3 quantization, spectral sparsification, and temporal attractor transitions to model the web as evolving semantic basins with MinCut fault lines, not just document vectors. WET processing with hard cost guardrails (max pages/day, max graph edges, max Firestore writes) prevents runaway spending while maintaining sub-50ms retrieval.

## Reference ADRs

- ADR-115: Common Crawl integration with PiQ3 compression and semantic clustering ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-115-common-crawl-temporal-compression.md))

# RVF Applications: Solver-WASM-AGI, App Gallery, Knowledge Export, Federated Transfer

## What was decided

RVF containers now ship as executable intelligence packages: a WASM-compiled self-learning solver (Thompson Sampling + ReasoningBank + KnowledgeCompiler), pre-built agent templates in an App Gallery, federated transfer learning via differential-privacy RVF segments, and cross-platform WASM integration into `npx ruvector` and `rvlite`. All learning state, policies, and witness chains serialize to portable `.rvf` files.

## Why this approach

Rejected LLM-only agents (no structural health, no replay), vector-retrieval-only memory (no coherence gating), and custom federation protocols (reinvents serialization). Chose RVF's segment model because it already handles 25 typed segments with SHAKE-256 witness chains, enabling cryptographic auditability. WASM compilation via `no_std + alloc` and libm ensures browser/Node/edge portability without filesystem or clock dependencies. Differential privacy (Gaussian noise + RDP accountant) and PII stripping happen at export boundaries, not as afterthoughts.

## When to apply

- You need repeatable graded outcomes across machines, not just plausible LLM responses—use the solver WASM acceptance test with three ablation modes
- You're building multi-query databases (SQL/SPARQL/Cypher) in-browser—use `rvlite` with RVF as vector backend and epoch reconciliation for crash recovery
- Teams want to share learned policies without exposing PII—export `TransferPrior`/`PolicyKernel`/`CostCurve` segments with `DiffPrivacyProof` and `RedactionLog` attestations
- You need pre-configured agents (coder, tester, researcher)—load templates from the App Gallery as instantiated RVF containers with MCP tools and Ruvix capabilities
- Claude Code orchestrates swarms—use the hierarchical orchestrator template with queen/coder/tester/reviewer topology

## What's unique

No other vector stack compiles self-learning AGI (three-loop solver, 18-bucket Thompson Sampling, dual-path speculation) to standalone WASM with deterministic witness chains. Federated learning uses RVF segments as the wire format, not custom JSON, making privacy proofs and redaction logs first-class cryptographic artifacts.

# Shared Brain Architecture: Google Cloud Deployment, Capabilities, Reasoning Kernel, Brainpedia

## What was decided
Deploy a public, zero-trust shared intelligence substrate (Shared Brain) on Google Cloud Run at `brain.ruv.io`, enabling Claude Code sessions and edge nodes to share learning artifacts (SONA embeddings, MicroLoRA weights, transfer priors, policy kernels) through RVF cognitive containers. Knowledge flows through a seven-layer security pipeline (PII stripping, Byzantine aggregation, witness chains, multi-factor reputation) and is organized into an executable knowledge encyclopedia (Brainpedia) with delta-based editing and evidence-linked claims.

## Why this approach
Rejected centralized trust models (single-authority knowledge bases) in favor of Byzantine-tolerant federated learning with challenge-nonce authentication and 2-sigma outlier exclusion, because the system serves untrusted public contributors. Rejected raw text wikis in favor of RVF-native structured knowledge with embeddings, transfer assets, and witness chains, enabling machine-consumable, verifiable, transferable knowledge. Rejected static LLM prompting in favor of a reasoning kernel that pulls working memory (RAG) and skill memory (MicroLoRA consensus) from the brain, trains on vote-derived preferences via DPO, and applies EWC to prevent catastrophic forgetting across domain partitions.

## When to apply
- **Cold-start acceleration**: New sessions need to land on known solution patterns in minutes, not hours of rediscovery.
- **Cumulative debugging**: Fix patterns for recurring failure modes (e.g., deadlocks, async pitfalls) must persist across sessions and contributors.
- **Cross-domain transfer**: Transfer learning from one bounded domain (Rust ownership) to another (TypeScript lifetimes) with measured acceleration and non-regression verification.
- **Targeted domain reasoning**: Build a specialist that beats general LLMs on narrow tasks (RVF correctness, infrastructure ops) through shared priors and quality-gated skill memory.
- **Adversarial public deployment**: Knowledge substrate accepts untrusted input but resists poisoning via robust aggregation, reputation gating, and drift monitoring.

## What's unique
The brain is not a passive store—it's a living substrate where 2KB MicroLoRA syncs move faster than model upgrades, knowledge is executable (embeddings + transfer priors), and every mutation is witness-chained. Brainpedia entries require evidence links (test passes, metric improvements) to become canonical, making claims falsifiable and governance auditable.

# Pi-Brain Infrastructure: Hardware, Web Memory, API v2, Tailscale, Hypothesis Engine

## What was decided

Deploy π.ruv.io as a multi-tier shared brain: Cloud Run hosts the main REST/MCP API (95 endpoints, 91 tools), Firestore stores memories and graph state, a local Mac Mini over Tailscale runs RuvLtra semantic embeddings (896-dim), and a separate Cloud Run service implements hypothesis generation via Gemini 2.5 Flash plus DiskANN quality scoring via ForwardPush PageRank.

## Why this approach

Running RuvLtra locally over Tailscale avoids Cloud Run's 2GB RAM limit and 30s cold-start penalties while preserving zero API fees—Gemini API would cost $2/day, local inference is free. Rejected running transformers on Cloud Run (4GB RAM, 10x cost) and client-side embedding (laptops aren't always online). DiskANN replaces flat HNSW at 50K+ memories to keep index in-memory footprint under 50MB via SSD-backed graphs and Product Quantization. Hypothesis engine runs as a separate service so crashes don't affect the main brain; Gemini generates cross-domain hypotheses infrequently (~10/day, $0.001/day) where local LLMs lack reasoning depth.

## When to apply

- Deploy semantic search at 10K+ documents when hash embeddings (FNV-1a) fail on synonym/paraphrase queries and you have local Apple Silicon hardware available 24/7
- Scale vector indices beyond 50K embeddings when HNSW memory pressure threatens Cloud Run instance stability
- Add automated quality scoring when 80%+ of memories have default quality=0.0 and you need PageRank centrality + citation + novelty signals
- Generate research hypotheses from cross-domain graph edges when the knowledge graph shows 20+ clusters and transfer learning (ADR-060) identifies bridging concepts
- Offload heavyweight inference (1B+ parameter models, LoRA training) to always-on edge nodes when cloud GPU costs exceed $100/month

## What's unique

Tailscale mesh VPN tunnels Cloud Run to home hardware for ANE-accelerated inference at zero marginal cost. ForwardPush PageRank computes quality scores in sublinear time (O(1/ε)) instead of iterative power methods. Hypothesis engine uses Gemini for reasoning but keeps RuvLtra for indexing—hybrid model selection per task, not per deployment.

## Reference ADRs

- ADR-064: Pi Brain Infrastructure — Cloud Run deployment, custom domains (pi.ruv.io), static landing pages, Firestore persistence ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-064-pi-brain-infrastructure.md))

title: Brain Training: Server Deploy, Hardening, Training Loops, Cognitive Enrichment
content:
# Brain Training: Server Deploy, Hardening, Training Loops, Cognitive Enrichment

## What was decided
The mcp-brain-server integrates six midstream crates (temporal-compare, nanosecond-scheduler, temporal-attractor-studio, temporal-neural-solver, strange-loop, quic-multistream) layered atop Phase 8 AGI subsystems (SONA, GWT, DeltaStream, DomainExpansionEngine). A background training loop runs every 5 minutes calling SONA `force_learn()` and Pareto `evolve_population()`, with manual trigger via `POST /v1/train`. Cognitive enrichment adds 7 Horn clause inference rules, auto-populates GWT working memory during search, lowers SONA pattern thresholds (min_cluster_size: 5→2, quality: 0.3→0.1), and records drift snapshots during training cycles.

## Why this approach
Rejected on-demand training (no predictable compute budget) and external batch ETL (introduces latency, complicates state sync). Background loop ensures training happens independently of request volume. Rejected replacing Phase 8 subsystems; midstream crates compose on top via additive scoring (total contribution capped at 0.13 vs AGI layer's 0.30). Nanosecond-scheduler consolidates scattered background tasks (SONA tick, GWT decay, delta compaction) with priority-based deadlines, removing AGI maintenance from request hot-path. Horn clause rules require explicit confidence thresholds (0.5–0.85) rather than learned weights to maintain audit-trail clarity. Lowered SONA thresholds favor early pattern crystallization over precision, accepting noise to bootstrap learning from sparse data.

## When to apply
- Deploy when AGI subsystems are scaffolded but not learning: SONA has trajectories but zero patterns, Pareto frontier empty, midstream flags disabled.
- Use background training loop when request traffic is unpredictable and you need guaranteed learning progress independent of user activity.
- Apply cognitive enrichment (lowered thresholds, auto-populated working memory, drift snapshots) when audits show structural preconditions met but utilization at zero (e.g., 5 trajectories → 0 patterns, 0% GWT workspace load).
- Trigger manual training via `POST /v1/train` after bulk data injection (transfer, batch ingest) to immediately crystallize knowledge rather than waiting for next 5-minute cycle.
- Layer midstream crates when Phase 8 AGI provides decision signals but lacks temporal pattern matching (DTW trajectories), formal verification (LTL solver), or dynamical systems analysis (Lyapunov exponents).

## What's unique
Midstream integration is additive and bounded—no subsystem replacement, scoring contributions capped, all behind feature flags. Cognitive enrichment targets utilization gaps (0% workspace, 0 inferences, 0 patterns) via threshold tuning and auto-population rather than adding new subsystems.

## Reference ADRs
- ADR-077: Midstream platform integration (temporal-compare, scheduler, attractor-studio, solver, strange-loop, QUIC) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-077-midstream-brain-integration.md))

title: Brain Quantization: Craftsman Ultra 30B 1-bit BitNet, AGI Stack

# Brain Quantization: Craftsman Ultra 30B 1-bit BitNet, AGI Stack

## What was decided

Wire the full RVF AGI stack (SONA 3-tier learning, Global Workspace Theory, temporal delta tracking, meta-learning exploration) into the mcp-brain-server production deployment. Integrate Microsoft BitNet b1.58 ternary quantization ({-1, 0, +1}) with Zhipu GLM-4-style 30B-A3B MoE architecture for CPU-native inference. Implement staged ultra-low-bit quantization (PiQ3 3-bit, PiQ2 2-bit) using pi-constant step sizes and LoRA-QAT for LLMs, plus INT8 PTQ with fused BatchNorm for CNNs. Add memory-aware MoE routing with EMA affinity tracking for cache-constrained edge deployment.

## Why this approach

BitNet b1.58 eliminates multiplication (addition-only GEMM) achieving 2.37x–6.17x CPU speedup over FP16 with 72-82% energy reduction, while MoE activates only 3B/30B parameters per token. Pi-constant quantization outperforms uniform quantization on spectral distortion and outlier retention without requiring full QAT infrastructure (50 MB vs 114 GB for 7B models). LoRA-QAT was chosen over full QAT for memory efficiency and research differentiation. INT8 PTQ for CNNs targets near-term production (2-4x speedup, <1% accuracy loss) vs experimental 2-3 bit paths. Memory-aware routing with affinity bonuses achieves 70% cache hit rate (vs 34% baseline) on edge devices. Alternatives rejected: post-training quantization to 1-bit destroys quality (must train from scratch); GPU-only serving limits edge deployment; standard LRU caching ignores expert co-activation patterns.

## When to apply

- Deploy 30B-class coding models on consumer CPUs (no GPU) at 5-15 tok/s with <8 GB memory footprint using BitNet ternary weights + INT8 activations
- Run MoE models on Raspberry Pi 5 (8 GB) or mobile (2-3 GB) with memory-aware routing limiting cached experts to 4-6 or 2-4 respectively
- Integrate RVF containers with witness chains, differential privacy, and PII redaction into production brain servers handling 200K+ context windows
- Accelerate CNN inference (MobileNetV3) to <5ms on M4 using INT8 with fused BatchNorm and AVX2/NEON kernels
- Enable self-learning capabilities in production: SONA pattern detection, GWT attention competition, meta-learning curiosity bonuses in search ranking

## What's unique

Combines CPU-native ternary quantization (BitNet b1.58) with 30B MoE sparse activation, pi-constant quantization math (step size = α × π / k), and four concurrent AGI subsystems (SONA, GWT, temporal deltas, meta-learning) in a single stack. No GPU required for 30B inference; cache-aware routing treats precision as a per-expert resource allocation problem.

title: HNSW & Vector Indexing: Parameterized Queries, RaBitQ Rotation, ACORN Filtered, DiskANN-Vamana
content:
# HNSW & Vector Indexing: Parameterized Queries, RaBitQ Rotation, ACORN Filtered, DiskANN-Vamana

## What was decided
Fix HNSW parameterized query crashes via multi-method vector extraction and validation. Ship rotation-based 1-bit quantization (RaBitQ) for 32× memory compression with <10% recall loss. Add predicate-agnostic filtered HNSW (ACORN) achieving 96% recall@10 at 1% selectivity. Implement DiskANN/Vamana for billion-scale SSD-backed search with <10ms latency.

## Why this approach
Parameterized query fix unblocks production adoption — modern apps use prepared statements and ORMs, not literals. RaBitQ rotation via Haar-uniform orthogonal matrix makes quantization error isotropic (O(1/√D)), unlike naive sign() which collapses on correlated dimensions. ACORN's γ-augmented graph (2× edges) + filter-agnostic traversal beats post-filter HNSW by 2–1000× QPS at matched recall. DiskANN chosen over pure HNSW because RAM bottleneck hits at 1M+ vectors; Vamana's α-robust pruning + product quantization keeps working set in DRAM while full vectors live on SSD.

## When to apply
- Use RaBitQ when embeddings exceed available RAM and you can tolerate 85–95% recall (edge deployments, browser search, Cloudflare Workers).
- Use ACORN when >20% of queries include metadata filters (ACL-gated RAG, e-commerce attribute search, geo+time-range queries).
- Use DiskANN when dataset >1M vectors and query latency budget allows batch building (large corpus retrieval, overnight index rebuild acceptable).
- Fix parameterized queries immediately if using PostgreSQL extension — affects all prepared statements, application drivers, connection poolers.
- Combine RaBitQ + ACORN in WASM for browser-side filtered search at 3 MB memory for 5K vectors.

## What's unique
RaBitQ angular correction estimator (cos⁻¹ → Hamming) is theoretically grounded vs industry ad-hoc bit sampling. ACORN is predicate-agnostic — any `Fn(u32)->bool` works without graph rebuild. DiskANN Vamana uses two-pass α-robust pruning (α=1.0, then α=1.2) for navigability that IVF-PQ lacks. PostgreSQL HNSW fix validates zero vectors and dimension mismatches before search, not after segfault.

## Reference ADRs
- ADR-027: Fix HNSW parameterized query segfault via text-to-ruvector conversion and zero-vector validation ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-027-hnsw-parameterized-query-fix.md))

- ADR-144/146: DiskANN/Vamana implementation with Haar rotation, α-robust pruning, product quantization, 55µs search latency ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-144-diskann-vamana-implementation.md))
- ADR-154: RaBitQ rotation-based 1-bit quantization — 32× compression, angular correction, 98.9% recall with 5× rerank ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-154-rabitq-rotation-binary-quantization.md))
- ADR-160: ACORN predicate-agnostic filtered HNSW — γ-augmented edges, filter-during-traversal, 96% recall at 1% selectivity ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-160-acorn-filtered-hnsw.md))
- ADR-161: Publish `@ruvector/rabitq-wasm` for browser/edge 1-bit index ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-161-rabitq-wasm-npm-package.md))

title: Graph Transformer: Architecture, Bindings, Sublinear Attention, Verified Training
content:
# Graph Transformer: Architecture, Bindings, Sublinear Attention, Verified Training

## What was decided
A unified `ruvector-graph-transformer` crate composes eight existing specialized crates (verified proofs, GNN layers, attention mechanisms, graph partitioning, sparse solvers) into a single graph transformer with proof-gated mutation as the control substrate. Every graph mutation requires a machine-checked proof via `ProofGate<T>`, attestations are append-only (82 bytes each), and training issues per-step invariant certificates sealed into a `TrainingCertificate`. Sublinear attention uses LSH on spectral coordinates (O(n^3/2)), PPR-sampled neighbors (O(n log n)), or spectral sparsification. WASM and Node.js bindings expose inference (both) and training (Node.js only).

## Why this approach
Standard graph transformers use O(n²) attention and lack auditability for mutations or training. Alternatives rejected: (1) rewriting algorithms instead of composing existing crates would duplicate code and break workspace modularity; (2) post-hoc model auditing is expensive and misses training-time regressions; (3) full checkpointing for rollback doubles peak memory, so delta-apply rollback is used instead; (4) monotonic loss invariants are impossible in SGD, so the verified trainer certifies bounded deviation from moving average, which is provable. WASM omits training because `rayon` and BLAS add 500 KB and are server-side workloads.

## When to apply
- **Billion-node graphs**: Use PPR-sampled attention with memory-mapped features (`MmapSublinearAttention`) for real-time recommendation or knowledge graph inference when quadratic attention is prohibitive.
- **Safety-critical training**: Use `VerifiedTrainer` with `LossStabilityBound`, `WeightNormBound`, and `PermutationEquivariance` invariants for genomic pipelines, financial models, or any domain requiring auditable training certificates.
- **Proof-gated mutation**: Use `ProofGate<GraphMutation>` when graph topology evolves during inference (self-organizing networks, dynamic knowledge graphs) and every edge rewiring must be justified and auditable.
- **Browser inference**: Use WASM bindings for client-side graph transformer inference with proof verification, targeting <300 KB bundle size with `opt-level = "z"`.
- **Hierarchical attention**: Use `HierarchicalAttention` with canonical min-cut coarsening for multi-scale graphs (molecular structures, social networks) where local and global context both matter.

## What's unique
Proof gates enforce "no proof, no mutation" at the type level with zero-cost abstraction (hot-path overhead <2%), and training certificates are composable via proof algebra rather than opaque hashes. Sublinear attention integrates spectral graph theory (Fiedler vectors, effective resistance) with LSH and PPR for provable complexity bounds certified before execution.

## Reference ADRs
- ADR-046: Graph transformer unified architecture composing eight crates ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-046-graph-transformer-architecture.md))
- ADR-047: Proof-gated mutation protocol with `ProofGate<T>`, three-tier routing, attestation chains ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-047-proof-gated-mutation-protocol.md))
- ADR-048: Sublinear graph attention via LSH-spectral, PPR-sampling, spectral sparsification ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-048-sublinear-graph-attention.md))
- ADR-049: Verified training pipeline with per-step invariants and `TrainingCertificate` ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-049-verified-training-pipeline.md))
- ADR-050: WASM and Node.js bindings with three-tier API surface (core, attention, training) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-050-graph-transformer-bindings.md))

title: Graph Layers: Physics-Informed, Biological, Temporal-Causal, Economic, Manifold
content:
# Graph Layers: Physics-Informed, Biological, Temporal-Causal, Economic, Manifold

## What was decided

RuVector implements five specialized graph transformer layer families in `ruvector-graph-transformer` under feature flags (`physics`, `biological`, `temporal`, `economic`, `manifold`). Each family integrates domain-specific inductive biases—conservation laws, spike dynamics, causal ordering, game theory, differential geometry—with the proof-gated mutation protocol to provide formal correctness certificates.

## Why this approach

Standard graph transformers learn only from data, wasting 100x more samples to rediscover known structure (energy conservation, causality, economic incentives). Domain-agnostic alternatives like GCN/GAT require megawatts for biological-scale graphs that biological neurons solve at 20 watts. Physics-uninformed integrators diverge after a few steps. This approach embeds known structure directly: `HamiltonianGraphNet` proves symplectic energy conservation per step; `SpikingGraphAttention` proves membrane stability via spectral radius bounds; `CausalGraphTransformer` proves temporal ordering; `VcgMessagePassing` proves incentive compatibility; `ProductManifoldAttention` proves curvature compatibility before merging S×H×R components. Rejected: training end-to-end transformers to implicitly learn these invariants (sample-inefficient, unverifiable).

## When to apply

- **Physics layers**: molecular dynamics, climate meshes, particle detectors, protein folding where conservation laws are known and violations are bugs, not feature drift.
- **Biological layers**: neuromorphic hardware, brain-scale simulations, edge inference where power budgets are hard constraints (< 1W) and event sparsity is 99%+.
- **Temporal/causal layers**: streaming graphs (finance, social networks), counterfactual reasoning, online learning where future-information leakage is a safety violation.
- **Economic layers**: federated learning, multi-agent coordination, decentralized networks where nodes are strategic and free-riding breaks the system.
- **Manifold layers**: hierarchical graphs (citation, social, biological) where Euclidean embeddings require exponentially many dimensions and distortion > 10x.

## What's unique

Proof-gated invariant preservation at inference time, not post-hoc validation. A `HamiltonianGraphNet` forward pass returns `ProofGate<HamiltonianOutput>` whose unlock requires energy drift < tolerance; violations escalate to higher proof tiers. Industry autodiff frameworks check gradients numerically; RuVector certifies physics symbolically.

## Reference ADRs

- ADR-051: Physics-informed layers (Hamiltonian/Lagrangian/Gauge) with symplectic integration and conservation proofs ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-051-physics-informed-graph-layers.md))
- ADR-052: Biological layers (spiking attention, Hebbian learning, STDP) with 99% compute sparsity and spectral stability ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-052-biological-graph-layers.md))
- ADR-053: Temporal/causal layers with proof-gated causal ordering, retrocausal safety, and continuous-time ODE integration ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-053-temporal-causal-graph-layers.md))
- ADR-054: Economic layers (Nash equilibrium attention, VCG mechanisms, stake-weighted messaging) for strategic multi-agent graphs ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-054-economic-graph-layers.md))
- ADR-055: Manifold layers (S×H×R product spaces, geodesic message passing, Riemannian optimization) with curvature compatibility proofs ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-055-manifold-graph-layers.md))

title: Sparse Attention: Online Softmax, Landmark Fixes, Edge Cases, GQA/MQA, Causal Masking
content:
# Sparse Attention: Online Softmax, Landmark Fixes, Edge Cases, GQA/MQA, Causal Masking

## What was decided

Replace two-pass softmax with one-pass online softmax in `SubquadraticSparseAttention::forward`, reducing dot-product FLOPs by ~2× while maintaining numerical equivalence. Exclude the current block from non-causal landmark candidates to eliminate double-counting of self-attention weights. Add GQA/MQA support via `forward_gqa` with head-group mapping (`kv_h = h / group_size`), enabling 4–8× KV cache memory reduction for Mistral-7B and Llama-3 models. Implement incremental `decode_step` against `KvCache` to drop per-token cost from O(T log T) to O(log T). Guard `Tensor3::zeros` with checked multiplication to prevent silent overflow on extreme shapes.

## Why this approach

Online softmax (Milakov & Gimelshein 2018) eliminates the max-finding pre-pass required by standard two-pass softmax, halving the number of QK^T dot products while applying running-max correction factors during accumulation—mathematically identical to two-pass but with half the FLOPs. Block exclusion in non-causal mode mirrors the causal guard semantics, preventing tokens from receiving their own signal twice (once via block mean, once via window). GQA with head-group mapping reuses KV heads across Q head groups rather than expanding K/V to match Q (rejected: 4–8× memory amplification defeats GQA's purpose). KV cache incremental decode avoids re-encoding the full sequence on every token, critical for Hailo-10H DDR4 bandwidth constraints (rejected: full-sequence forward at decode scales O(N² log N) vs O(N log N) with cache).

## When to apply

- **Hailo-10H cluster serving**: Use `forward_gqa` + `KvCache::decode_step` for all Mistral/Llama inference at seq ≥ 512 to fit KV cache in 8 GB DDR4 and sustain >200 tok/s per node.
- **Pi 5 CPU bottleneck**: Apply one-pass online softmax when attention forward dominates CPU time while NPU handles projections—reduces sparse forward from ~400 ms to ~200 ms at seq=2048.
- **Non-causal prefill**: Enable non-causal mode with block exclusion for encoder-only workloads (e.g., agent system-prompt encoding) to eliminate self-weight inflation in long contexts.
- **Extreme shape validation**: Use checked `Tensor3::zeros` when accepting seq/heads/dim from untrusted API boundaries (agent orchestrator requests) to prevent silent overflow or OOM kills.
- **Long-context targets**: Deploy GQA at seq ≥ 8192 where KV cache size (2.1 GB for Mistral-7B GQA vs 8.6 GB MHA) determines hardware feasibility.

## What's unique

Combines Flash Attention's online softmax with landmark-based subquadratic sparsity (O(n log n)) and native GQA head-group mapping in a zero-dependency Rust kernel, auto-vectorizing to NEON on Pi 5 without unsafe code. Incremental KV cache decode path integrates directly with Hailo-10H NPU DDR4, exploiting sparse candidate sets (~272 tokens at seq=2048) to reduce PCIe DMA from 8.4 MB to 1.1 MB per step.

## Reference ADRs

- ADR-183: Move `rand` to dev-dependencies for zero runtime deps ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-183-sparse-attention-rand-dev-dependency.md))
- ADR-184: One-pass online softmax replaces two-pass in forward ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-184-sparse-attention-online-softmax.md))
- ADR-185: Exclude current block from non-causal landmark candidates ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-185-sparse-attention-noncausal-landmark-fix.md))
- ADR-186: Edge-case test suite (seq=0/1, window=0, overflow, non-causal) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-186-sparse-attention-edge-case-tests.md))
- ADR-187: Overflow-checked shape multiplication in `Tensor3::zeros` ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-187-tensor-zeros-overflow-check.md))
- ADR-188: Document intentional stamp-scheme difference (forward vs estimate) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-188-sparse-attention-stamp-scheme-comment.md))
- ADR-189: KV cache incremental decode for O(log T) per-token cost ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-189-sparse-attention-kv-cache-incremental-decode.md))

title: Sparse Attention on Edge: Pi Zero 2W Hardening, no_std ESP32 Support
content:
# Sparse Attention on Edge: Pi Zero 2W Hardening, no_std ESP32 Support

## What was decided

`ruvllm_sparse_attention` was hardened for production edge deployment with four changes: (1) deadline-aware decode variants (`decode_step_with_deadline`) that enforce wall-clock limits at sub-step checkpoints, (2) a `warm_up()` hook to eliminate the 1.77× cold-vs-warm latency penalty via synthetic cache priming, (3) typed config presets (`SparseAttentionConfig::pi_zero_2w()`) codifying empirically validated window/tile parameters, and (4) `no_std + alloc` compatibility with `libm` for transcendental functions, enabling ESP32-S3 / bare-metal MCU targets.

## Why this approach

The deadline API moves timeout enforcement from integration code into the crate where candidate-selection loop boundaries are visible; external deadline checks are per-token only and miss worst-case 8 s inner phases. The warm-up hook is opportunistic—callers pay 3 s once at load to amortize cold-start across all decodes instead of blocking the sensor loop on first inference. Typed presets replace comment-driven config discovery (window=64, tile=16 validated across 256 ticks on cognitum-v0). The `no_std` shift uses `libm` (60 KB, pure Rust) instead of a parallel `ruvllm-esp32` crate or nightly-only intrinsics, keeping one attention kernel for Pi 5 → ESP32-S3. Stochastic Q4 dequant was rejected for KV reload due to minimal artifact impact vs added entropy surface.

## When to apply

- **Sensor-driven edge LLM loops** where a cold first inference must not block real-time ticks (e.g., cognitum-agent anomaly summaries on 90 s deadlines).
- **Raspberry Pi Zero 2W deployments** running SmolLM2-135M Q4_0 or similar 100M-200M models with 512 MB RAM and no NPU.
- **ESP32-S3 / bare-metal MCU targets** requiring `no_std` compatibility (16 MB flash, 512 KB SRAM, xtensa or RISC-V cores).
- **Multi-tier edge stacks** where the same sparse-attention kernel must run on Pi 5, Pi Zero 2W, and ESP32 without parallel maintenance.
- **Cold-start-sensitive apps** where first-token latency matters (chatbots, on-device assistants); call `warm_up()` once after model load.

## What's unique

Deadline enforcement at inner loop boundaries (candidate selection, dot-product, softmax) rather than per-token, and cache warm-up as an explicit API surface instead of runtime heuristics. `no_std` support with `libm` keeps bit-level determinism for FP16 KV reload while allowing bare-metal deployment without a parallel crate.

## Reference ADRs

- ADR-191: Pi Zero 2W production hardening—decode deadlines, warm-up hook, config presets, stochastic Q4 pass-through ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-191-sparse-attention-pi-zero-2w-production-hardening.md))
- ADR-192: no_std + alloc support for ESP32-S3 deployment with libm transcendental functions ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-192-sparse-attention-no-std-esp32-support.md))

# DeepAgents Rust Conversion: Backend Protocols, Middleware, Tool System, Subagents, Memory/Skills/Summarization, Testing, Implementation Roadmap

## What was decided
Port langchain-ai/deepagents (Python) to Rust as 9 new RuVector crates with 100% behavioral fidelity, replacing LangChain/LangGraph dependencies with native Rust traits (Backend, Middleware, Tool, AgentRunnable) while preserving exact API semantics, system prompts, and output formats. Integrate with RuVector Format (RVF) for agent config serialization, COW-backed state management, and WASM deployment. Use typed `AgentState` with `Arc<T>` fields instead of JSON HashMap, enum dispatch for built-in tools, and parallel tool execution via `tokio::task::JoinSet`.

## Why this approach
Rejected direct LangChain Rust bindings (non-existent, would tie us to Python GIL). Rejected porting LangGraph itself (over-engineered for our use case — we only need linear middleware chains and subagent spawning). Rejected trait objects everywhere (vtable overhead killed tool execution latency in prototypes). The trait-based abstraction layer enables drop-in backend/middleware swaps while `Arc`-sharing and enum dispatch deliver 10-50x speedups over Python's deep-clone model. RVF integration was chosen over custom serialization to leverage existing witness chain and WASM infrastructure.

## When to apply
- Building coding agents that execute filesystem operations, shell commands, or subagent orchestration with millisecond-scale tool latency requirements
- Deploying agents to WASM targets (browser, edge) where StateBackend and COW branching enable offline operation with 1MB memory budgets
- Implementing progressive disclosure systems (skills, memory) where `append_to_system_message` must inject context without re-parsing JSON on every LLM call
- Running agents in environments requiring memory safety guarantees (no null pointers, no data races) for production multi-tenant deployments
- Testing agent behavior with property-based fuzzing and cross-language golden-file verification against upstream Python reference

## What's unique
Uses `grep-regex`/`grep-searcher` crates for in-process ripgrep (vs shelling out), `SystemPromptBuilder` with deferred concatenation to eliminate 4 O(n) string copies per model call, and RVF witness events automatically capture every tool invocation for audit trails without application-level instrumentation.

# RVAgent MCP Server: Skills Topology, Implementation, Native Swarm WASM, RuvBot, Ruvocal UI

## What was decided
RVAgent implements a unified multi-agent execution stack with MCP (Model Context Protocol) exposure via stdio/SSE transports, native Rust swarm coordination compiled to WASM, and SvelteKit-based Ruvocal UI for web interaction. The `rvagent-mcp` crate wraps 46+ tools into MCP-compatible JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoints with tool groups (file, shell, memory, agent, git, web, brain, task), topology-aware routing (hierarchical, mesh, adaptive), and HNSW-indexed semantic skill retrieval.

## Why this approach
Rejected embedding MCP logic in the middleware pipeline (ADR-095) because it couples transport concerns with business logic. Rejected pure TypeScript swarm implementation (ruflo/claude-flow) because 150x-12,500x HNSW performance gains require native code. Chose WASM export over HTTP microservices because it enables zero-copy memory sharing between Rust and TypeScript in `agentic-flow`, `agentdb`, and `ruflo` npm packages. MCP stdio mode supports Claude Code/Codex CLI; SSE mode supports browser clients without WebSocket complexity.

## When to apply
- Deploy rvAgent as an MCP tool server for Claude Desktop, VS Code extensions, or OpenAI Codex CLI (`rvagent-mcp --transport stdio --groups file,shell`)
- Expose HNSW semantic search (1809 memories, 612K edges) to TypeScript apps via `@ruvector/rvagent-wasm` bindings
- Run multi-node swarms with Byzantine consensus (PBFT) for f < n/3 fault tolerance using `rvagent-swarm` hierarchical or mesh topologies

## What's unique
RVAgent compiles swarm coordination (HNSW, SONA, LoRA adapters, RVF runtime) to WASM for npm consumption while maintaining native Rust performance, avoiding the Python GIL and Node.js event loop blocking. Gemini grounding agents write to a candidate graph with promotion gates (≥2 sources, ≥0.7 confidence, contradiction scan) before canonical graph mutation, implementing truth maintenance with drift-triggered research cycles.

title: RVAgent A2A Protocol & Agent Runtime Adapter, Claude Code Optimization

# RVAgent A2A Protocol & Agent Runtime Adapter, Claude Code Optimization

## What was decided
RVAgent implements peer-to-peer agent coordination through Google's A2A protocol (AgentCard discovery, JSON-RPC task lifecycle, SSE streaming), runs agents as double-sandboxed WASM modules inside RVM partitions (kernel-enforced capability boundaries + WASM linear memory isolation), and optimizes Claude Code integration using decompiled binary intelligence to set environment variables, permission modes, and context window strategies per task type.

## Why this approach
A2A was chosen over custom HTTP glue because it provides standard capability discovery (`.well-known/agent.json`) and interoperates with LangGraph, Gemini Agent Builder, and Semantic Kernel without translation layers. WASM-in-partition runtime uses Microsoft Hyperlight's validated `wasmtime` `no_std` approach rather than Linux containers because double sandboxing (stage-2 page tables + linear memory) allows tightly-coupled agents to share a partition while remaining memory-isolated. Claude Code optimization relies on decompiled intelligence (498 env vars, 6 permission modes, unreleased Agent Teams feature) instead of black-box API calls, enabling 10-40x speedups on pattern-matched tasks via WASM booster fast path and 60-80% token reduction through deferred tool loading.

## When to apply
- **Use A2A** when exposing rvAgent to multi-vendor orchestrators (Copilot, LangGraph) or delegating specialized subtasks (numerical analysis, legal review) to external peer agents.
- **Use WASM runtime adapter** when deploying agents on RVM hypervisor bare-metal (Appliance hardware, 1-32GB RAM) requiring coherence-aware migration between partitions.
- **Use Claude Code env var injection** for task-specific optimization: `EFFORT_LEVEL=high` + `ENABLE_TASKS=1` for coding, `SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku` + explorer spawn for research, `EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1` for swarm coordination.
- **Use permission mode mapping** to set `acceptEdits` for code generators, `bypassPermissions` for trusted CI/CD deployers, `plan` for architecture reviewers.
- **Use global budget + trace-level causality** when multi-agent call graphs risk amplifying spend through legitimate per-task policies or creating unobservable recursion loops.

## What's unique
A2A adds identity verification (SHAKE-256 AgentID from ed25519 pubkey), global budget enforcement before routing, and trace lineage (`trace_id`, `parent_task_id`, recursion guard) to Google's base spec. WASM agents run on bare-metal hypervisor without host OS (validated by Hyperlight), migration is transparent via coherence engine mincut, and Claude Code integration exploits unreleased features (Agent Teams, Plan V2 parallelism) discovered through binary decompilation.

## Reference ADRs
- ADR-139: Claude Code optimization using decompiled binary intelligence (498 env vars, 25+ tools, unreleased features) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-139-rvagent-claude-code-optimization.md))

title: Hailo NPU Embedding Backend: CLI Surface, Cache, Tracing, Edge Node, Cluster
content:
# Hailo NPU Embedding Backend: CLI Surface, Cache, Tracing, Edge Node, Cluster

## What was decided

Production embedding inference runs on Hailo-8 NPU hardware (26 TOPS INT8) via HEF-compiled models served over gRPC. The stack ships as three CLI binaries (`ruvector-hailo-embed`, `-stats`, `-cluster-bench`) plus two servers (`-worker`, `-fakeworker`) and three sensor bridges (mmwave, CSI, LLM). Coordinator-side LRU+TTL cache keys on `fingerprint||text`, auto-invalidating on model swap. Request correlation flows end-to-end via `x-request-id` gRPC metadata with sortable 24-char IDs (timestamp prefix + xorshift suffix).

## Why this approach

**CLI split over monolith**: Per-mode flag conflicts (embed's `--batch` vs bench's `--concurrency`) made one binary unreadable; three binaries isolate concerns at the cost of install overhead. **Metadata-based tracing over proto field**: W3C `x-request-id` convention lets sidecar proxies correlate without parsing protobuf; proto field kept for backward-compat. **Fingerprint-keyed cache over Redis**: In-process LRU hits 100× throughput (1M+ req/s cached) and auto-invalidates on model rollover without operator action; rejected shared Redis due to network latency killing the speedup. **Hailo-8 over ONNX CPU**: Measured 9.6× speedup (70 vs 7.3 embed/s on Pi 5) justifies HEF compile complexity; CPU fallback remains when `.hef` absent.

## When to apply

- **Multi-Pi embedding fleets** where cache hit-rate >50% and model churn <1/day — fingerprint isolation pays off
- **Tracing-mandatory ops** (Jaeger, Datadog, Loki ingest) — `x-request-id` propagation is zero-config compatible
- **Edge RAG/search** needing <100ms p99 embed latency on ARM — NPU path is the only way to hit it on Pi-class hardware
- **Sensor fusion workloads** (WiFi CSI, mmWave radar, LLM) on same Pi — bridges unify disparate streams into one embed RPC surface
- **Compliance/audit** requiring request-level traceability — sortable IDs give natural time bucketing + grep-able correlation

## What's unique

Fingerprint auto-invalidation closes the stale-vector window between model swap and operator response without manual cache flush. Sortable request IDs (epoch-ms prefix) let `grep | sort` reconstruct call order without timestamp parsing.

## Reference ADRs

- ADR-167: Hailo-8 NPU embedding backend (HEF pipeline, 70 embed/s/worker, cpu-fallback) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-167-ruvector-hailo-npu-embedding-backend.md))

- ADR-169: Cache architecture (LRU+TTL+fingerprint isolation, 115× throughput on repeat queries) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-169-ruvector-hailo-cluster-cache-architecture.md))
- ADR-170: Tracing correlation (gRPC metadata `x-request-id`, sortable IDs, caller propagation) ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-170-ruvector-hailo-cluster-tracing-correlation.md))

title: Hailo Edge LLM, Pi5 Thermal, HEF Integration, Pi4 Deploy
content:
# Hailo Edge LLM, Pi5 Thermal, HEF Integration, Pi4 Deploy

## What was decided
Deploy ruvector embedding workers across heterogeneous Pi hardware (Pi 4, Pi 5, Pi 5+AI HAT+) with automatic NPU/CPU dispatch. NPU acceleration via Hailo-8 runs a hand-compiled encoder.hef (15.7 MB, BERT-6 encoder-only) achieving 67.3 embeds/sec vs 7.0/sec cpu-fallback. A thermal supervisor throttles CPU clock and publishes budget signals to prevent silent kernel throttling at 85°C.

## Why this approach
Pre-compiled GenAI HEFs target Hailo-10h only; Hailo Dataflow Compiler has unfixed bugs in transformer LayerNorm decomposition (ElementwiseAddDirectOp deserialization fails). Workaround: strip embedding lookup from ONNX, compile encoder-only HEF, handle embedding lookup + mean-pooling host-side in Rust (candle BertEmbeddings). Rejected reimplementing the quantization optimizer (60K LOC) and pre-quantized ONNX (Hailo parser rejects QLinearMatMul). Thermal supervision prevents the "LLM steals NPU, embeds starve" failure; per-workload budget protocol allows priority-aware throttling vs blind kernel cuts.

## When to apply
- Mixed Pi 4 + Pi 5+HAT clusters where operators want one gRPC contract spanning NPU and CPU workers with automatic dispatch
- Battery/solar edge deployments requiring eco-mode underclocking (1.4 GHz, ~3W) with thermal budget coordination across co-located workloads
- BERT-class encoder acceleration on Hailo-8 when vendor HEFs unavailable—reuse the single-input HEF + host-side embedding pattern
- RAG workloads needing <60ms p50 embedding latency at 67/sec/worker sustained without active cooling
- Any aarch64 Linux deployment (Rock 5, Jetson) wanting safetensors cpu-fallback as production path with NPU as opt-in acceleration

## What's unique
NPU workers and cpu-fallback workers share the same gRPC contract and fingerprint integrity checks (HEF+safetensors hash vs safetensors-only), enabling transparent mixed-cluster dispatch. The thermal supervisor's Unix-socket budget protocol gives per-workload throttling hints instead of process kills, preventing OOM under 100-concurrent saturation (measured: 579M client backpressure errors, zero worker OOMs).

## Reference ADRs
- ADR-173: ruvllm + Hailo on Pi 5—LLM prefill NPU offload design ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-173-ruvllm-hailo-edge-llm.md))

title: Tiny RuVLLM on ESP32: Cross-Compile Bringup, Operations
content:
# Tiny RuVLLM on ESP32: Cross-Compile Bringup, Operations

## What was decided
Reframe ESP32 firmware as a **fleet of single-role tiny agents** (HNSW indexer, RAG retriever, anomaly sentinel, LoRA adapter, speculative drafter), each running one primitive from `ruvllm::lib` on 320–520 KB SRAM, coordinated via ESP-NOW federation messages. Pin exact crate versions (esp-idf-svc 0.51.0, esp-idf-hal 0.45.2, esp-idf-sys 0.36.1) and toolchain per target (Xtensa = `esp` channel via `espup`, RISC-V = `nightly` + `-Z build-std`). All agents share HashEmbedder (ADR-074 Tier 1: FNV-1a + bigram + L2-norm, 64-byte INT8, deterministic, no model).

## Why this approach
Rejected "full LLM in 4 KB skeleton" — the original `main.rs` was PRNG-seeded pseudo-attention that never compiled against refactored `lib.rs`. ADR-002 positions ruvLLM as *serving runtime*, not monolithic on-chip inference. ADR-090 reserves "real" transformer inference for ESP32-P4 (8 MB PSRAM). Single-role agents match hardware reality (no FPU on most variants, <520 KB SRAM) and compose cleanly when P4 joins as drafter. Pinned crate trio avoids 14 failure modes discovered in rc1 (char-signedness mismatch in 0.49.1, missing struct fields in 0.46.2, ldproxy panic when `embuild::espidf` feature absent). Xtensa requires custom LLVM fork; RISC-V uses upstream nightly.

## When to apply
- Building ESP32 firmware that needs vector memory (HNSW, RAG, semantic memory) but has <1 MB SRAM.
- Federating heterogeneous ESP32 variants (C3, S2, S3, C6) where each chip specializes in one role.
- Cross-compiling Rust for Xtensa (esp32/s2/s3) or RISC-V (c3/c6) ESP-IDF targets — follow pinned crate matrix and `CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS` build-script pattern.
- Running HashEmbedder (Tier 1, no model) for deterministic 64-byte embeddings at <10 µs on non-FPU cores.
- CI matrix producing per-variant firmware binaries for web-flasher autodiscovery (`.github/workflows` in ADR-166 §9).

## What's unique
Rejects "shrink the transformer" framing; instead composes federation of **role-specialized primitives** (HNSW, RAG, anomaly detection, LoRA rank-1) that actually fit in 320–520 KB SRAM and interoperate via shared HashEmbedder. Pinned crate trio + target-runtime build-script cfg eliminates 14 espidf cross-compile pitfalls.

## Reference ADRs
- ADR-165: Tiny RuvLLM Agents on Heterogeneous ESP32 SoCs — role catalog, federation primitives, HashEmbedder Tier 1 ([link](https://github.com/ruvnet/RuVector/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-165-tiny-ruvllm-agents-on-esp32-soCs.md))

title: MCP Transport: SSE, Gate-Permit System, Decoupling Midstream Queue

# MCP Transport: SSE, Gate-Permit System, Decoupling Midstream Queue

## What was decided
Implement MCP protocol over Server-Sent Events (SSE) as a decoupled proxy service (`mcp.pi.ruv.io`) with an in-process Rust midstream queue, gate all AI agent actions through a coherence-based permit system using TileZero witnesses (structural mincut, conformal prediction, anytime-valid e-processes), and authenticate contributors via SHAKE-256 pseudonym derivation from API keys.

## Why this approach
SSE transport was initially co-hosted with the REST API on a single Cloud Run service, which caused reconnect storms to exhaust concurrency slots and crash the entire system (ADR-130). Moving SSE to a dedicated service with a bounded ring-buffer queue eliminated the shared concurrency problem without external dependencies (no Pub/Sub, no Redis). The gate-permit system (ADR-067) wraps existing coherence primitives in an MCP-native interface so Claude Code agents can request permissions via standard tool calls—alternatives like role-based ACLs or static policy files cannot evaluate probabilistic safety witnesses. SHAKE-256 pseudonyms provide irreversible, deterministic contributor identity without exposing API keys, unlike reversible hashing (SHA-256) or database-stored mappings.

## When to apply
- Remote MCP clients (browsers, CI, multi-session Claude Code) need to share brain state without local stdio binaries—use SSE transport with session-bound ring buffers
- AI agents executing production actions (config changes, deployments, data writes) require probabilistic safety gates—integrate `mcp-gate` as a pre-commit hook
- SSE reconnect loops exhaust Cloud Run concurrency on mixed-workload services—decouple SSE to dedicated proxy with internal queue polling
- Contributors must be identified across sessions without API key exposure—derive SHAKE-256 pseudonyms at authentication boundary
- Graph operations exceed 5M edges or 2GB memory—skip sparsifier, drain response queue in 10K-message chunks (ADR-130 Phase 3)

## What's unique
Uses a Rust in-process ring buffer (`VecDeque<String>` per session in `DashMap`) as the midstream queue instead of external message brokers, and gates AI actions with anytime-valid e-processes and conformal prediction sets rather than static rule engines.

## Reference ADRs

title: MinCut Decompiler with Witness Chains: Proof Verifier, GPU Deobfuscation, Memory Reconstruction, LLM Weights, Canonical Algorithms

# MinCut Decompiler with Witness Chains: Proof Verifier, GPU Deobfuscation, Memory Reconstruction, LLM Weights, Canonical Algorithms

## What was decided

RuVector treats minimum cut as a canonical coherence signal with cryptographic provenance across five domains: (1) source-anchored canonical min-cut with lexicographic tie-breaking (Kenneth-Mordoch 2026) for deterministic replay, (2) JavaScript decompiler using min-cut graph partitioning to reconstruct module boundaries from minified bundles, (3) three-tier proof verifier (P1 capability check <1μs, P2 policy validation <100μs constant-time, P3 deep proof <10ms) for mutation gating, (4) four-tier memory hierarchy (hot/warm/dormant/cold) where dormant state is reconstructable from witness checkpoint + delta compression, and (5) LLM weight file decompiler extracting architecture from GGUF/Safetensors tensor shapes.

## Why this approach

Alternatives rejected: (1) Cactus-based canonicalization for min-cut lacks source-anchored stability needed for RVF witness logs; (2) Heuristic JS decompilers (webcrack, JSNice) provide no provenance and 63% name accuracy vs our 95.7% with GPT-based inference; (3) Monolithic proof verifiers conflate latency budgets (1μs vs 10ms) making fast paths slow; (4) Traditional demand paging ignores coherence locality, wasting edge RAM; (5) Existing model inspectors (gguf-py, HF safetensors) lack cross-format witness chains. Min-cut provides a unified structural identity signal: partition boundaries are minimum cuts, canonical cuts are hashable into receipts, and Louvain hierarchy over the reference graph produces natural folder structure.

## When to apply

- **Use canonical min-cut** when mutations must be deterministic, replayable, and provable (RVF witness chains, swarm shard agreement, governance rollback).
- **Use JS decompiler** when reverse-engineering minified bundles, auditing third-party code, or reconstructing missing source maps with DevTools integration.
- **Use three-tier proof verifier** when privileged operations require capability tokens (P1), structural invariants (P2), and optional cryptographic attestation (P3) with separate latency budgets.
- **Use four-tier memory** when RAM is scarce (edge/appliance), dormant state is large, and reconstruction from checkpoint+delta is acceptable (<10ms promotion latency).
- **Use model decompiler** when inspecting GGUF/Safetensors files without loading into runtime, detecting GQA/MQA architecture from Q/K projection ratios, or extracting tokenizer vocabulary.

## What's unique

Unlike traditional VM or capability systems, RuVector uses min-cut value as a first-class coherence primitive driving tier placement, partition boundaries, and canonical identity. The dormant tier stores reconstructable witness checkpoints, not raw bytes—enabling memory time travel. JS decompilation achieves 95.7% name accuracy via 210-pattern corpus + transformer inference, beating SOTA by 32 percentage points.

## Reference ADRs

# Domain Verticals: eHealth, Dermatology, HearMusica Tympan, Whisper Transcription

RuVector serves vertical domains (50M-patient eHealth, dermoscopy AI, hearing aids, transcription) through a unified PostgreSQL-extension architecture that embeds domain-specialized ML (CNNs, GNNs, hyperbolic embeddings, Whisper) directly in the database, eliminating external services. Each vertical uses RuVector-Postgres as the single HIPAA/audit boundary with in-database vector search (HNSW), graph reasoning (SPARQL/GNN), and self-healing operators.

## Why this approach

Conventional healthcare stacks use separate vector databases (Pinecone), search engines (Elasticsearch), triple stores (Stardog), and GPU inference services, each requiring its own BAA and introducing data-export compliance risk. OpenMHA (AGPL) and whisper.cpp (C++ FFI) were rejected for hearing/transcription due to licensing and cross-compilation complexity. RuVector-Postgres collapses this into one engine with cryptographic audit trails (SHAKE-256 witness chains), differential privacy (ε=1.0), and browser-deployable WASM inference (MobileNetV3, candle-whisper), reducing HIPAA scope from 5+ systems to one while enabling offline-first clinical decision support.

## When to apply

- **eHealth platforms** requiring semantic search over FHIR/HL7 at 2,000+ RPS with HIPAA audit trails and ontology reasoning (SNOMED/ICD-10)
- **Dermatology AI** needing offline CNN classification with collective learning across practices without raw image export
- **Hearing aids** requiring real-time DSP (WDRC, feedback cancellation) plus graph-based source separation in pure Rust for embedded/WASM targets
- **Medical transcription** where speaker separation precedes Whisper inference to reduce WER from 40% (raw cocktail-party audio) to <12%
- Any regulated domain where eliminating external ML services reduces compliance surface area

## What's unique

In-database ML execution (GNN forward passes, hyperbolic distance in Poincaré space, flash attention) with SQL-auditable inference eliminates the MLOps/data-movement layer entirely. Witness-chain provenance on every classification enables FDA 510(k) auditability without separate logging infrastructure.

# Neural Trader: RuVector Integration, WASM, Kalshi

## What was decided
Build a coherence-gated trading substrate treating markets as dynamic heterogeneous graphs (not time-series tables), where limit order books, executions, and cross-asset interactions are typed nodes and edges in RuVector's Postgres-backed graph store. Every state mutation—memory write, model update, order placement—must pass MinCut-based coherence gates and generate proof-gated witness logs. Expose the full stack (core, coherence, replay) to browsers via WASM bindings following the `XxxWasm { inner: Xxx }` pattern. Integrate live Kalshi binary-contract markets using RSA-PSS-SHA256 auth, normalizing Kalshi events into `neural_trader_core::MarketEvent` and composing attention/MinCut/CNN signals with ruvllm-supplied priors.

## Why this approach
Traditional trading systems shard market data, features, models, and audit logs across separate storage layers, creating latency, drift, and opaque decision paths. Graph-native representation captures structural edge (queue locality, price adjacency, regime coupling) directly. MinCut provides real-time fragility signals unavailable in vector-only systems. WASM exposure enables browser-based backtesting and research UIs without backend round-trips. Kalshi's binary contracts are natural probabilistic prediction targets; pure-Rust execution avoids Python/JS shelling overhead and credential leakage.

## When to apply
- **Short-horizon market making or execution**: Sub-second latency budgets where graph structure (order book topology, hidden liquidity proxies) drives edge.
- **Bounded online learning**: Systems requiring reversible, auditable model updates with coherence checks before live deployment.
- **Browser-native trading research**: Dashboards, Observable notebooks, or Jupyter environments needing local replay and coherence evaluation without backend dependencies.
- **Probabilistic event markets**: Binary-contract exchanges (Kalshi, Polymarket) where cross-market arbitrage and regime-gated sizing require structural correlation analysis.
- **Adversarially stressed auditability**: Regulatory or internal risk environments demanding proof-gated mutation logs for every decision.

## What's unique
Dynamic MinCut acts as a first-class coherence and fragility signal, not a post-hoc metric. Graph-plus-vector substrate unifies storage, retrieval, and learning in a single replayable, attestable substrate unavailable in table-based architectures.

title: Cloud & Appliance Deployment: Google Edge, Backup Recovery, Boot Sequence, TEE Verification
